While automation promises efficiency gains, our workforce is the backbone of Riverton Industries, and without proper reskilling, we risk both employee morale and long-term productivity. Strong data infrastructure is the foundation for any AI initiative, so it deserves significant investment. The innovation lab is exciting but should be tempered by practical needs, and employee support, while important, can be partially integrated into training programs. This allocation ensures we build capability from the ground up rather than rushing into automation that could leave people behind.

I'd recommend a balanced but forward-leaning allocation: 30% to Workforce Training, 25% to Automation, 20% to Data Infrastructure, 15% to Innovation Lab, and 10% to Employee Support. The reasoning is that AI transition will fail if employees aren't equipped to work alongside new systems—training is the linchpin. Automation delivers quick efficiency gains that can fund other initiatives, while robust data infrastructure is the foundation for any AI success. The Innovation Lab keeps us competitive long-term, and Employee Support, though smallest, is essential for morale and retention during disruption.

I'd tell them that while automation and data infrastructure are tempting because they promise quick efficiency gains, I believe the most critical investment is in our people. We can build the fanciest AI systems, but without a skilled, motivated workforce to run them, we're just wasting money.
